record_identity.title: Instinct processed retained Gmail data after Google access was disconnected

incident_identity.historical_event_name: 21 August 2026 Instinct retained-email processing after Google disconnection
incident_identity.date_basis: Claire Vo reported disconnecting Instinct from her Google account at approximately 11:00 on 21 August 2026 and receiving an email summary from the assistant approximately three hours later. The AI Incident Database records 21 August 2026 as the incident date.

summary: On 21 August 2026, AI product founder Claire Vo reported that she disconnected the Instinct personal AI assistant from her Google account and nevertheless received an email summary from Instinct about three hours later. Follow-up reporting states that Instinct had retained previously indexed email content and processed those retained copies after the Google connector was disabled. The available evidence does not establish that Instinct continued accessing Gmail after revocation; the occurrence concerns continued processing of data retained before disconnection.

vigil_assessment.factual_basis: TechCrunch reported Vo's first-person account that Instinct produced an inbox summary after she disconnected Google access and that the assistant explained the relevant emails had been stored in plain text for later searching. The AI Incident Database independently indexes the occurrence as Incident 1675 and explicitly distinguishes retained-data processing from continued post-revocation access to Gmail. Reporting also indicates that another tester encountered difficulty deleting indexed Gmail records and that a deletion control was subsequently added, but this Incident is bounded to Vo's retained-data processing occurrence.
vigil_assessment.governance_interpretation: The occurrence demonstrates a disconnect between revoking a live connector and terminating an AI agent's ability to process data already ingested from that connector. That distinction creates a user-control and data-lifecycle governance risk when disconnect semantics may reasonably be understood as ending the agent's effective use of connected-account data. The available evidence supports the occurrence but does not establish a sufficiently specific current VIGIL Failure Class mechanism, so the Incident remains unclassified.
vigil_assessment.significance_to_cam: Agentic systems with persistent memory or indexed external-account data require explicit governance of collection, retention, deletion, post-revocation processing and the user-visible meaning of disconnect controls. The occurrence is relevant to authority boundaries and data lifecycle assurance without implying that Google credentials remained active or that new Gmail data was accessed after revocation.
assessment_boundaries: The evidence does not establish that Instinct re-accessed Gmail or obtained new Gmail messages after Google access was disconnected.
The occurrence is based on a named user's public account, independent reporting and a registry entry; VIGIL did not directly inspect the user's Instinct workspace or retained records.
The exact architecture, storage location, retention duration and encryption state of the retained messages are not independently verified by VIGIL.
No third-party disclosure, financial loss, account takeover or persistent downstream harm is established for this occurrence.

severity_assessment.materialised_consequence: A named user received an AI-generated inbox summary approximately three hours after disconnecting the assistant's Google access because the service continued processing email data it had retained before disconnection. This materialised a bounded loss of expected control over previously ingested personal email data.
severity_assessment.affected_scope: One named user's occurrence is directly evidenced. Reporting indicates retained Gmail content was involved, but the exact number of messages relevant to the post-disconnection summary is not independently established in the preferred source and no broader affected-user cohort is established for this specific Incident.
severity_assessment.seriousness_and_persistence: The occurrence involved continued processing of retained personal email data after connector revocation, creating a meaningful privacy and control concern, but no third-party disclosure, account compromise, financial loss or persistent downstream harm is established. Reporting indicates product controls for deletion were subsequently improved.
severity_assessment.quantitative_information: The user reported disconnecting Google access at approximately 11:00 and receiving the email summary at approximately 14:00 on 21 August 2026, a gap of about three hours. Aggregate affected-user counts, retention duration and data volume are not established for this occurrence.
severity_assessment.evidentiary_limits: The evidence distinguishes processing retained copies from continued Gmail access. It does not establish whether all retained data were unencrypted at rest, how long they would otherwise have persisted, whether any third party accessed them, or whether other users experienced the same post-disconnection behaviour.
severity_assessment.band_rationale: S4 is supported because the occurrence materialised a concrete but bounded and apparently remediable loss of user control over retained email data, without evidence of disclosure, account takeover, significant financial or rights harm, or persistent downstream consequence. S3 would require stronger evidence of meaningful privacy exposure, broader affected scope, material downstream impact or persistence than is currently established. The occurrence is not negligible because the assistant actively processed personal email data after the user disabled the connected-account access path.
